content:
incidentbot: HIGH | 17:13 UTC — streaming responses error-rate spike observed for hosted API (prod-usw2). Pager sent to @emma.

emma: acked. I'm onboarding — collecting initial metrics. Observed ~18% error rate on streaming endpoints (chunked responses); non-streaming text/generate seems fine so far. Starting with scope and impact.

mike: +1. Customers on web-chat and a few integration customers reported truncated streams. No 5xx spike on non-streaming routes. Logs show websocket disconnects and `GRPC_STREAM_RESET` in front of runtime.

jess: adding quick triage checklist below so agents can respond consistently. Use the macros (drafts) further down when replying to customers.

paul: quick note — putting a brief status page draft here so incidents team can push if needed.

emma: Triage checklist for support agents (use before sending any customer-facing message):
1) Confirm affected customer: ask for request_id or example timestamp (UTC). If they can't provide, ask for a single example time within last 30 minutes.
2) Check customer route: is request using streaming API (chunked/stream) vs. non-stream? Streaming only impacts many reports.
3) Collect diagnostic snippet from customer (copy/paste):
   - request_id header
   - approximate client timestamp
   - client-side error message (if any)
4) Run internal quick checks (support shell):
```
# check recent errors for a customer id
rg "request_id=|GRPC_STREAM_RESET" /var/log/redwood/requests/*.log | tail -n 100
# streaming runtime pod logs (k8s)
kubectl -n inference logs deployment/stream-runtime -c runtime --since=15m | rg "GRPC_STREAM_RESET" | head
# check LB health
curl -s https://infra-metrics.internal/streaming/errors?window=15m | jq '.'
```
5) If you see consistent `GRPC_STREAM_RESET` for that request_id, escalate to oncall-sre with the following payload: subject + attachments (logs snippet, request_id, client region, SDK version).

mike: Customer quick-ack templates (Zendesk / Intercom). Short, empathetic, actionable. Paste the macro and use variables.

Zendesk macro — initial-ack-streaming:
```
Hi {{customer.name}},

Thanks for the report — we see issues affecting streaming responses right now. We're actively investigating. Can you please share a sample request_id or a timestamp (UTC) for the request so we can correlate logs? We expect a follow-up in ~30 minutes. Apologies for the interruption.

— Redwood Support
```

Intercom suggested reply — streaming-ack:
```
Thanks for flagging this. We're aware of a problem with streaming responses and investigating. If possible, could you send a request_id or the approximate time (UTC) of the failed request? We'll follow up with an update within 30–45 minutes.
```

jess: Customer-facing status page blurb (short):
```
Incident: Streaming responses experiencing partial failures in US West region.
Impact: Some streaming sessions may disconnect or return truncated output. Non-streaming generation unaffected.
Status: Investigating — engineering is diagnosing gateway/runtime interaction. Next update: ~30 minutes.
```

emma: Internal status update (for #incidents channel):
- Impact: ~18% of streaming calls in prod-usw2; affecting web chat and SDK streaming clients.
- Suspected surface: load-balancer/gateway performing socket resets upstream of runtime (seen `GRPC_STREAM_RESET`).
- Actions: collecting pod logs, rolling restart of streaming gateway is a low-risk mitigation if we confirm stuck connections.
- Mitigation plan: If error-rate >25% for 15m, trigger rolling restart of stream-gateway (canary 5% -> 20% -> remainder), monitor errors.

paul: Mitigation playbook snippet (ops runbook):
```
1) Notify customers via status page + support macros.
2) Take a single gateway canary restart (5% nodes):
   kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/stream-gateway --selector=canary=true
   wait 2m, observe error rate.
3) If errors drop by >50% in 10m, continue staged restart: 20% then 100%.
4) If errors persist or spike, roll back and escalate to kernel/network infra team.
```

mike: Hand-off template for next oncall/support shift (copy into the handoff thread):
```
Handoff -> Oncall: {{next_oncall}}
Time window: started 17:13 UTC
Current status: Investigating. Streaming error rate ~18% (prod-usw2).
What we have: logs with GRPC_STREAM_RESET, suspected gateway socket resets.
What to do: run the quick-checks, consider canary restart of stream-gateway if error-rate rises >25%.
Outstanding asks: correlate example request_id from customers and attach logs.
Next update ETA: 30 minutes from now or earlier if mitigation executed.
```

jess: Suggested escalation message to SRE (if needed):
```
SRE pager: observed elevated GRPC_STREAM_RESET in prod-usw2 streaming endpoints since 17:13 UTC. Error-rate ~18% (15m window) and client disconnects reported. We recommend network/gateway check and, if safe, a controlled restart of stream-gateway canary. Attaching logs and sample request_ids: [log-snippet].
```

emma: Operational notes — things to avoid in customer messages:
- Don’t promise a timeframe for full resolution unless mitigation completed.
- Avoid deep technical jargon (no need to mention kernel TCP settings to customers).
- Use “partial failures to streaming” + “non-streaming unaffected” phrasing.

support-bot: Suggested Slack reaction taxonomy for this thread: :rotating_light: for triage milestones, :white_check_mark: for mitigations, :hourglass_flowing_sand: for waiting on SRE.

mike: I'm entering the draft Zendesk macro now and tagging support leads. If anyone has a cleaner phrase for the status page, drop it here; otherwise I'll push the short blurb Paul posted.

jess: One last quick checklist for agents responding live (TL;DR):
- Send initial ack macro (ask for request_id).
- Run quick internal checks.
- If matched logs → escalate to oncall-sre with logs.
- Update customer with short note after mitigation attempt (success/failure) within 30–45m.

emma: thanks team. I'll run the canary if errors jump or after SRE gives the greenlight. Leaving this thread pinned for handoff.

paul: tagging @oncall-sre and @netops. Also adding a short template for statuspage follow-up once we have a mitigation result:
```
Update: Engineering performed a staged restart of stream-gateway canary at 17:42 UTC. Error-rate reduced by ~70% in the following 10 minutes. Continuing staged rollout.
```

incidentbot: Thread closed to new automated alerts (manual updates only).
